content.title: Treasury cancels $21 million in Booz Allen contracts, blaming Trump tax return leak
content.summary: The Treasury Department cut ties with Booz Allen Hamilton on Monday and announced that it was canceling $21 million in federal contracts with the consulting giant because one of its ex-employees previously leaked President Donald Trump’s tax returns to the press.

thumbnail.caption: MCLEAN, VIRGINIA - JUNE 20: The Booz Allen Hamilton Headquarters on June 20, 2024 in Mclean, Virginia. Booz Allen is a government and military consulting company that provides management, technology and engineering services to public and private sector organizations and nonprofits. content.title: Why Booz Allen Stock Took a Beating After Treasury Contract Cancellations
content.summary: Shares of defense technology and consulting firm  Booz Allen  Hamilton fell 8% Monday after the Treasury Department announced that it was cancelling all its contracts, valued at $21 million, over leaked tax returns.  Monday’s cuts reignite fears that the company is “at risk of being made an example of by the Administration,” Stifel analyst Jonathan Siegmann, said.  “Today’s statement by the [Treasury] Secretary is a set-back.”

content.title: Why Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) Stock Is Falling Today
content.summary: Shares of government consulting firm Booz Allen Hamilton (NYSE:BAH) fell 9.2% in the afternoon session after the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced it canceled all contracts with the consulting firm.

content.title: Booz Allen Hamilton Stock Slides After Treasury Drops Contracts
content.summary: The Treasury Department is canceling all its contracts with Booz Allen Hamilton, Secretary Scott Bessent said on Monday.  Booz Allen had 31 contracts with the Treasury, with total annual spending of $4.8 million, the department said.  The department flagged the taxpayer data released by former Booz Allen employee Charles Littlejohn.

content.title: Booz Allen Contracts Canceled by Treasury Department
content.summary: The Treasury Department said it currently has 31 contracts with Booz Allen totaling $4.8 million in annual spending and $21 million in total obligations.

content.title: Why Shares of Booz Allen Hamilton Are Sinking Today
content.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent cancelled all department contracts with Booz Allen Hamilton, citing a broader effort to eliminate 'waste, fraud, and abuse.'
